Figure 1. Large-scale real-world multi-agent experiment of TOPOMA. Left: RTK-based ground-truth trajectories overlaid on a satellite

                            Abstract                                              laboration. TOPOMA explicitly models the spatial topo-
                                                                                  logical structure of the scene and tightly couples it with
Multi-agent 3D reconstruction, as a key technology for                            end-to-end representation learning, thereby jointly solving
large-scale VR/AR, robot swarms, and digital twins, has                           core challenges such as inter-agent spatial alignment and
attracted growing attention. Recent end-to-end 3D recon-                          submap fusion. Concretely, we introduce topology skeleton
struction methods achieve strong performance in single-                           modeling and optimization, decentralized loop closure, and
agent scenarios, but they are difficult to directly extend                        topology-guided residual transport, and build upon them a
to multi-agent collaborative settings, where they often suf-                      fully distributed inference architecture in which each agent
fer from unstable tracking, excessive memory consumption,                         can independently store, reconstruct, and incrementally
and frequent loop-closure failures, thus failing to meet real-                    optimize its map while collaborating through lightweight
time and large-scale deployment requirements. To address                          topological information. Extensive experiments demon-
these issues, we propose TOPOMA, a real-time end-to-end                           strate that, compared with existing methods, TOPOMA
3D reconstruction framework tailored for multi-agent col-                         achieves consistently higher trajectory accuracy, recon-
                                                                                  struction quality, robustness, and topological consistency,
   * represents corresponding author. The first two authors contribute
equally to this paper.




                                                                          21784
showing superior adaptability and scalability.                       multi-agent field deployments, showing that TOPOMA
                                                                     outperforms current state-of-the-art single-agent and
                                                                     multi-agent baselines.
1. Introduction
Multi-agent 3D reconstruction underpins large-scale               2. Related work
VR/AR, robot swarms, and digital twins[9, 10, 18, 37].            Learning-based Pointmap Representations. Learning-
Single-agent coverage of complex environments is ineffi-          based pointmap representations have advanced monocu-
cient. Collaboration is required to share workload[17, 34],       lar dense 3D reconstruction by using deep learning mod-
accelerate exploration, and handle occlusions. Yet or-            els to predict dense 3D point clouds from image pairs or
ganizing and fusing observations in large, topologically          video sequences[1, 4, 19, 32, 40]. For instance, MASt3R-
complex scenes remains challenging. Existing end-to-end           SLAM[25] leverages a two-view 3D reconstruction prior
methods[3, 25, 31, 33], designed for a single camera and          for real-time monocular reconstruction without calibration
trajectory, perform well in single-agent settings but degrade     but faces computational and memory challenges in large-
in multi-agent scenarios, with unstable tracking, high mem-       scale environments. SLAM3R[23] uses a sliding win-
ory usage, and frequent loop-closure failures[5, 13, 16, 20].     dow mechanism for high-quality reconstruction but suf-
In practice, they either maintain independent maps with           fers from drift in longer sequences. TTT3R[3] improves

while loop closure still relies on local geometric heuristics     datasets still require further optimization. VGGT-Long[7]
without enforcing global topological consistency across           addresses memory and computational bottlenecks in large-
agents[36, 36, 39, 41].                                           scale sequences with a chunk and align framework but
    To address these limitations, we propose TOPOMA,              still demands high GPU memory. VGGT-SLAM[24] opti-
a real-time end-to-end map-first 3D reconstruction frame-         mizes over the SL(4) manifold for consistent submap align-

timization under communication constraints and heteroge-          struggle with collaborative challenges like inter-agent scale
neous trajectories. This skeleton summarizes connectivity         unification and resource distribution, motivating the need
and geometry between submaps from different agents and            for a multi-agent reconstruction framework grounded in

On top of this representation, three topology-driven com-         advancements in multi-agent collaborative reconstruction
ponents (topology skeleton construction, decentralized loop       have improved large-scale 3D tasks[5, 12, 26, 30, 35]. CP-
closure, and topology-guided residual transport) define a         SLAM[18] boosts collaboration using neural point-cloud

sages, so that corrections propagated along the skeleton al-      uses 3D Gaussian representations for multi-agent collabo-
low updates from one agent to benefit the others.                 ration and loop closure, though it has limitations in large-

                                                             21785
Figure 2. Overview of TOPOMA. Mapping: RGB observations are tokenized and aggregated to build a topology-aware skeleton, which
is unified with geometric cues to recover consistent structure and scale. Tracking: Agents perform local loop detection, update topology
constraints, and apply topology-consistent loop closures through frontend/back-end topology transformers, ensuring coherent multi-agent
pose estimation.The system runs fully distributed, allowing each agent to maintain local submaps while progressively achieving global
topological consistency.
